title: Pandora's box — Ritual and worship
summary: Pandora, the first woman, opened a jar releasing all evils into the world, leaving only hope inside. This study follows the myth into temples and festivals.
body:
Pandora, the first woman, opened a jar releasing all evils into the world, leaving only hope inside. Hesiod tells the tale in Works and Days.

Myths were not entertainment; they were scripts for ritual. Pandora's box was enacted in festivals, sacrifices, and mysteries that bound communities together and aligned human time with cosmic time. Viewed through a symbolic lens, Pandora's box is read for its images — what each figure and object stands for beneath the plot.

Where the myth was performed, it was believed with the body, not just the mind. A second sub-question concerns the historical kernel: what real events or places might stand behind Pandora's box. Related entries in this archive: Enuma Elish and Tuatha De Danann.
key_points: Ritual life of Pandora's box reconstructed.
